title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs
abstract: arXiv:2611.14545v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, and each token reads every weight from memory, so on edge devices, decoding is limited by memory bandwidth. 2:4 semi-structured sparsity keeps two of every four weights, but Apple-silicon GPUs have no sparse matrix hardware, so pruning helps only if a kernel actually reads fewer bytes. We present metalSPARSE, to our knowledge the first 2:4 sparse kernels for Apple GPUs, together with a fused decoder written in Metal. The kernels stream weights in compressed form and expand them in registers. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 2:4 sparsity on every decoder linear layer, decoding runs 3.6x faster than HuggingFace Transformers on PyTorch-MPS on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 1.52x faster than MLX on a 16 GB M4. The same engine on dense weights matches MLX, so the gain comes from the compressed weights, and sparsity delivers 97% of the speedup its byte reduction allows. Prompt pr

translated_title: metalSPARSE：面向Apple Silicon GPU的2:4半结构化稀疏GEMV内核
translated_abstract: 自回归大语言模型（LLM）逐个token地生成文本，而每个token都需要从内存中读取全部权重，因此在边缘设备上，解码速度受内存带宽限制。2:4半结构化稀疏保留每四个权重中的两个，但Apple Silicon GPU没有稀疏矩阵硬件，因此只有当内核确实读取更少的字节时，剪枝才能带来收益。我们提出了metalSPARSE，据我们所知这是首个面向Apple GPU的2:4稀疏内核，并配套用Metal编写了一个融合解码器。该内核以压缩形式流式读取权重并在寄存器中将其展开。在Qwen2.5-1.5B模型上对每个解码器线性层应用2:4稀疏后，解码在8 GB M2 MacBook Air上比PyTorch-MPS上的HuggingFace Transformers快3.6倍，在16 GB M4上比MLX快1.52倍。同一引擎在稠密权重上的性能与MLX相当，说明加速收益来自压缩权重，且稀疏性实现了其字节缩减所能带来的97%加速。提示处理……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: metalSPARSE是首个面向Apple Silicon GPU的2:4半结构化稀疏GEMV内核，通过以压缩形式流式读取权重并在寄存器中展开，使Qwen2.5-1.5B的解码在M2上比PyTorch-MPS快3.6倍、在M4上比MLX快1.52倍，实现了字节缩减所允许的97%加速。
en_tdlr: metalSPARSE is the first 2:4 semi-structured sparse GEMV kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs, which streams weights in compressed form and expands them in registers, accelerating Qwen2.5-1.5B decoding by 3.6x over PyTorch-MPS on M2 and 1.52x over MLX on M4, delivering 97% of the speedup its byte reduction allows.
